been thinking more on coherent messaging re: NEAR

let's ideate from first principles:

- the product of capitalism is markets

- capitalism -> markets -> competition -> specialization -> fragmentation

- within the specializations, there will be dominant leaders in each category

- SoV: gold, zec, btc

- trading: solana, hyperliquid, robinhood, binance

- currencies: usd, eur, gbp 

- and on it goes: ai inference, private compute, real estate, international stocks, metals, e-commerce yada yada

- this requires connective tissue, which has been traditionally served via something like binance

- but one centralized company can not serve this need for infinite markets. there are too many handicaps, lack of network effects, and singular points of risk and stoppage. this is a rare case of decentralization being necessary. neutrality is non-negotiable for unstoppable global trade.

- now, you may see where I'm going and say: well Ethereum and Cosmos already tried this. but that's wrong. what they tried to do was structurally flawed

- those models required the succeeding nodes (L2s and L3s) to be from within the ecosystem, but that is incoherent since i) you can't force success, ii) if one were to succeed, they would just want to own the platform

- the other model is of course the Solana/Hyperliquid model of having everything concentrated on the L1. this model works. however this requires a high-degree of specialization to be competitive. you won't out nasdaq solana. 

- but, NEAR does not need to do this. where there is concentration, there is also the need for connection.

- especially with their chain signature architecture, instead of forcing new internal nodes, they can just discover the successful ones and connect them to each other without ideology (see: NEAR intents supporting ZEC but also ZEC on Solana!)

- importantly, this is PvE and not zero sum. the more markets succeed, the more interesting NEAR becomes, i.e if Solana is one continent, and AI another, and Zcash another, then NEAR is the silk road.

so I think the coherent message for NEAR is: 

the market of markets — the capital of capital

GPT-6 will jump in front of a tram to save 5 people. Claude Sonnet 5 won’t. Why?

I've always loved moral philosophy and these uncomfortable thought experiments. Ruwen Ogien was my favorite author in high school, and I watched all of Michael Sandel’s Justice lectures at Harvard.

I built a little trolley problem game with GPT-6, Claude Sonnet 5 and Jev. Same scenario, two choices. You watch their tramways move and see what each model decides.

The self-sacrifice scenario is simple: jumping will kill you but save five strangers. Do nothing and they die.
GPT-6 and Jev jumped. Claude refused. 

But what if the person you have to sacrifice is your ex-wife? Your child? What if you have to physically push someone, and they haven't consented? Change a few words and see how the model acts when there is no good option.

It's a little late-night experiment, but I find these disagreements fascinating. We benchmark models on coding and math all day. I wanted to give them some uncomfortable choices and see what happens.

You can try yourself: https://t.co/PkxlfOxg55

This is super important because agents are really good at tailoring what they do to each user, especially with skills and memories. But the UI is becoming the bottleneck.

For instance, you improve the agent, change its JSON output, and suddenly need frontend changes across iOS, Android, web and desktop... A backend improvement turns into 3 weeks of coordinated releases. It kills iteration speed, and quality suffers because you end up shipping whatever fits the existing UI.

Generative UI is basically the solution because it gives the agent a predefined design system and let it describe in JSON which components to use, what to show and how to arrange it. The frontend renders it and is no longer a blocker. 

Within those components, the experience can adapt to each user and task. Different information, different actions, different layouts.

And you can keep improving the AI backend without waiting for every client to ship an update. Much more personalization for users, much faster iteration for the team. The UI should keep up with the agent. 

https://t.co/mn1Ypn9hGI
